title: Next.js: file-based routing, rendering modes and data fetching

videos.script:
In Next.js, the folders are the routes. Today the planner gets a page for each course, and then a harder question: when should each page be made?

{{folder}} First a folder with square brackets, a page inside it, and a loading file that Next.js wraps in Suspense for you.

{{fail}} Then two kinds of wrong: a course that does not exist, and a server that does not answer. Each gets its own file and its own screen, and a surprise about status codes.

{{modes}} Then the build's three marks: static, made once; partial, a shell made once with the rest streamed; and dynamic, made every time.

{{cache}} Then use cache. Course pages become files built ahead, and you will watch one keep saying sixty minutes after the data changed underneath it.

{{own}} And last, the bug that caching brings to your own changes, and the one line that fixes it: updateTag.
